preamble: Nasalization of [i] accompanied by lowering to close-mid [ẽ]. In the Swabian dialect of Horb, as recorded by Kauffmann (1890) and analysed by Kniess (2025), a vowel immediately before a nasal consonant is nasalized (Regressive Nasalization), and the high vowels lower in the process: short /i u/ surface as [ẽ õ], so that nasal vowels distinguish only two heights against four among oral vowels. Historical i in words like springen and bringen therefore surfaces as [ẽ].

examples.from: /i/ before a nasal, cf. Standard German spring! 'jump!'
examples.note: Regressive Nasalization: high /i/ lowers to [ẽ] before a nasal consonant; Kniess lists the rule as /i u/ → [ẽ õ].

examples.from: /i/ before a nasal, cf. Standard German bringt 'brings'
examples.note: Same lowering of /i/ to [ẽ] before a nasal (Kauffmann 1890, as analysed by Kniess 2025).

sources: Kniess, T. B. (2025). Nasalization and Nasal Vowels in the Swabian Dialect of Horb: A Phonological Analysis of Kauffmann 1890. PhD dissertation, Indiana University. https://scholarworks.iu.edu/dspace/items/f9ca887d-4125-46c1-8eb0-933b17f7d00c
context: Short or long stressed /i/ before a nasal consonant (Horb Swabian)
